errors.text: The proposed molecular-precursor intervention is not supported by the cited evidence for bulk Mg-transition-metal alloys; the evidence concerns metal sulfides, thin materials, or unrelated FeCoCrNi composites.
Dithiocarbamate thermolysis is likely to introduce sulfur and carbon and form sulfides or other secondary phases, directly undermining the claimed metallic single-phase-like alloy.
The falsification experiment does not compare intermediate temperatures within 800–1000 °C against the proposed 900 °C optimum, so it cannot establish a temperature optimum.
The experiment includes 1050 °C despite the stated upper processing constraint of 1000 °C.
Barrier performance is inadequately tested: corrosion in 3.5 wt% NaCl is omitted, and oxidation is evaluated at 600 °C rather than the relevant 900 °C condition.
Quantitative density and magnesium-loss boundaries are asserted without supporting evidence.
